newsitem.title: USA: U.S. OMB's Raines cautiously optimistic on budget.
newsitem.headline: U.S. OMB's Raines cautiously optimistic on budget.

text.p: White House Budget Chief Franklin Raines on Tuesday expressed guarded optimism about the potential to reach agreement with the Republican-led Congress on a plan to balance the budget.
"I'm cautiously optimistic we can make progress," Raines told the annual government affairs conference of America's Community Bankers.
He said that moving forward on a budget would require bipartisan cooperation.
Raines gave a measured response to a call by Senate Budget Committee Chairman Pete Domenici, delivered at the same banking conference, for President Clinton to change his budget dramatically.
"The President has put his budget on the table," Raines said, adding that Clinton was prepared to debate his budget and take into account any criticism.
The White House budget director defended the Clinton administration record in consistently achieving greater budget deficit reduction than expected by both itself and the Congressional Budget office.
On Monday, the CBO said the Clinton budget plan would result in a $69 billion deficit in the year 2002.
